text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

-More than 2,200 people were arrested in 1996 for driving while under the influence of narcotics or other medical substances. Many people ignore warnings against driving on medical packaging, says Asbjoern Christophersen, leader of the state's toxin institute.
-The Health Ministry has decided to establish a national centre for HIV. Research in Norway in this area lags behind Sweden, Finland and Denmark, says Harald Moi, a manager at an Oslo Clinic.

-The Norwegian Association for Trade and Industry fears a further strengthening of the crown. The Central Bank must cut interest rates even more to calm interest for the Norwegian currency, chief economist Tor Steig says.
-Parliament will discuss the Schengen agreement in March as planned. The debate will not be postponed to await discussions inside the European Union, state secretary Oeystein Maeland says.

-Software house Sysdeco blames former manager Johns Jamne for poor financial results. Board members say they were not warned of the company's negative trend and therefore they cannot be blamed for giving the market wrong financial information.
